channel.title: Sparkstone Writing
channel.description: research and writing at Sparkstone LLC

item.title: A Background Remover That Doesn't Want Your Money
item.description: remove.bg is folding into Canva and free tiers shrink your photos. So I built one that runs in your browser, keeps your full resolution, and costs nothing to keep online.

item.title: Syncing Single Files Across Repos Without Ceremony
item.description: Shared files drift across repos. npm is too heavy and copying by hand makes a mess. filesync closes the gap with git merges, a one-line provenance header, and private-first regions.

item.title: Edible Neighborhoods
item.description: Evenings like this remind me why local matters, and that the best networks aren't always digital ones.

item.title: Arcanetable Insight
item.description: I checked in on an app I hadn't touched in over a year, and what I found had me utterly gobsmacked.

item.title: Build With People, Not In Isolation
item.description: A lot of us want to help by building good, useful things. But retreating to make the elegant, principled "right thing" in isolation is a trap. Software matters because it gets used, and the surest way to get it used is to build it with the people who need it.

item.title: CryptPad's URL Trick Is Genius
item.description: CryptPad stores the shared encryption key in the URL fragment, the part after the `#`. That one choice solves a whole class of secure-sharing problems.

item.title: OpenMLS Looked Like the Perfect Answer, Until It Wasn't
item.description: On paper, it checked all the boxes. In practice, I ran into a hard constraint that made it the wrong fit for what I was trying to build.
